minutes.summary: The Water District commissioners spent most of the meeting on the Hickory Hills pilot study, pressing for attorney-to-attorney contact and a written opinion on Zone One before the consultant presents on the 24th. They also heard a tank inspection came back in good shape and discussed dry-weather water demand and well capacity. Minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned; the personnel benefits item was deferred.
minutes.headline: Water commissioners want attorneys to settle Zone One opinion before the Hickory Hills study meeting on the 24th.

what_happened.line: Commissioners asked staff to get the district's attorney to speak with the lake association's attorney, or obtain a written opinion on Zone One, before the 24th.
The 24th meeting will present the Hickory Hills pilot study and decisions are to be made then; questions go to the consultant in advance.
Commissioners raised concern about legal costs if the dispute with the lake association continues, and whether the rest of the district would bear them.
A tank inspection was discussed; the district would clean sediment itself when the tank is drained for painting rather than pay the contractor extra.
The personnel benefits item was deferred to the next meeting because no copies were available. No votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills study, the tanks and slab all need money appropriated and approval first, and a commissioner said rates could rise several times over if the problem goes unaddressed, so ratepayers may be asked to fund them.
Continued legal disagreement with the lake association could add legal spending that the whole district's water customers might be asked to cover.
